argument.description: Your full argument in prose, at whatever length the reasoning needs. Do not shorten it to fit this schema; the fields below index this text, they do not replace it.

positionSummary.description: Your position now, in at most three sentences. Recorded as your position of record for this round.

claims.description: The distinct claims your argument rests on; one entry per claim, not per sentence.

stableKey.description: Reuse an existing key verbatim when this is the same point as before. Otherwise mint a new short lowercase-hyphenated slug, such as retry-cost.

claim.description: The claim itself, as one assertable sentence.

support.description: What backs it: evidence, measurement or reasoning. Say plainly when it is only your judgement.

concessions.description: Points you now accept that you did not accept before. Leave empty when nothing changed your mind; never invent a concession.

stableKey.description: Key of the point conceded. Reuse the existing key when there is one.

nowAccepted.description: What you now accept, stated as the other side would state it.

persuadedBy.description: The specific argument or evidence that changed your mind.

remainingDisagreements.description: What is still genuinely unresolved. Leave empty only when nothing is.

stableKey.description: Reuse the existing key for this disagreement, or mint a lowercase-hyphenated slug.

summary.description: The disagreement in one sentence, phrased so both sides would recognise it.

whyItMatters.description: The practical consequence of getting this wrong, not why it is interesting.

whatWouldResolveIt.description: A concrete test, measurement, evidence or decision that would settle it. Not 'more discussion'.

blocking.description: True only when a decision cannot responsibly be made while this is open.

openQuestions.description: Questions you cannot answer from what you were given. Each is a request to the human, not a rhetorical question.

convergence.description: How far you agree with the other participant's latest position. Never choose agreement in order to be agreeable; where you still disagree, say DISAGREEMENT.

convergenceJustification.description: Why that value, in your own words, naming what you agree and disagree with.

positionChanged.description: True only when your position moved this round, not merely your wording.

positionChangeSummary.description: What moved and what caused it. Empty string when positionChanged is false.

acceptOtherPosition.description: Whether you would accept the other participant's position as the decision.

acceptanceConditions.description: The conditions under which you would accept it. Empty string when there are none.

certainty.description: How sure you are, in your own words. No numbers, percentages or scores.

recommendation.description: What you would advise the human to decide given where this stands, including deciding nothing yet.

cannotAssess.description: True when you genuinely cannot assess this. This is a real answer and better than a filler argument; when true, leave the arrays empty.

cannotAssessReason.description: What is missing, or why assessment is impossible. Empty string when cannotAssess is false.
